import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import json
import os

# Load the measurements data
df = pd.read_csv('input_data/measurements.csv')

# Compute the correlation matrix
corr = df.corr()

# Create a creatively coloured heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
cmap = sns.diverging_palette(220, 20, as_cmap=True)  # vibrant diverging colors
sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap=cmap,
            linewidths=.5, linecolor='gray', cbar_kws={'shrink': .5})
plt.title('Correlation Matrix of Measurements', fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure in both PNG and SVG formats
png_path = '/display_output/correlation_matrix.png'
svg_path = '/display_output/correlation_matrix.svg'
plt.savefig(png_path, dpi=300, format='png')
plt.savefig(svg_path, format='svg')
plt.show()

# ---- Output ----
print("Correlation matrix heatmap saved as PNG and SVG files.")
print(png_path)

# Load required libraries
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
df = pd.read_csv("input_data/measurements.csv")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute the correlation matrix
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
corr = df.corr()

# Show the numeric correlation matrix (intermediate result)
display(corr)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Plot a creatively coloured heatmap
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))

# Use a divergent palette with many colours for a vivid look
cmap = sns.diverging_palette(220, 20, as_cmap=True)

# Draw the heatmap; show correlation values on the cells
sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap=cmap,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    square=True,
    cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.6},
)

plt.title("Correlation Matrix of Measurements", fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Save the figure
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
png_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.png"
svg_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.svg"
plt.savefig(png_path, dpi=300)
plt.savefig(svg_path)

# Display the plot in the notebook
plt.show()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Output description and final result filename
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("A creatively coloured heatmap visualising the correlation matrix.")
print(png_path)   # final result: the filename of the .png file

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv("input_data/measurements.csv")

# Compute correlation matrix
corr = df.corr()

# Plot with a creative colormap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap=sns.diverging_palette(220, 20, as_cmap=True),  # creative divergent palette
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    cbar_kws={"shrink": .7}
)
plt.title("Creatively Coloured Correlation Matrix")
plt.tight_layout()

# Save both PNG and SVG
png_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.png"
svg_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.svg"
plt.savefig(png_path, format="png", dpi=300)
plt.savefig(svg_path, format="svg")
plt.show()

# Description of the result
print(f"Correlation matrix plot saved as PNG at {png_path}")

# Final result (only the filename)
print(png_path)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv("input_data/measurements.csv")

# Compute the correlation matrix (numeric columns only)
corr = df.corr()

# Create a creatively coloured heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap="Spectral",          # a vivid, multi‑coloured palette
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.7}
)
plt.title("Correlation Matrix of Measurements", fontsize=14)

# Save the figure in both PNG and SVG formats
png_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.png"
svg_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.svg"
plt.savefig(png_path, format="png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.savefig(svg_path, format="svg", bbox_inches="tight")

# Show the plot (Jupyter will render it)
plt.show()

# -------------------------------------------------
# Description of the result
print("Displayed a colourfully styled correlation matrix heatmap for all columns in measurements.csv.")

# Final output: the filename of the saved PNG image
print(png_path)

import pandas as pd

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

# Load the data

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)

# Compute correlation matrix

# --- Plot the correlation matrix ---
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))

# Use a creative colormap – here we combine two palettes for a vivid effect
cmap = sns.diverging_palette(220, 20, as_cmap=True)   # red‑blue diverging palette

sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap=cmap,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    cbar_kws={"shrink": .7},

plt.savefig(svg_path, format="svg")
plt.show()

# ---- Final outputs ----

print(png_path)   # final result: only the PNG filename

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

# 1. Load the data
data_path = "input_data/measurements.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_path)

# 2. Compute the correlation matrix
corr = df.corr()

# 3. Plot a creatively coloured heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
# using a vibrant colormap
sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap="turbo",          # a vivid colormap
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    cbar_kws={"shrink": .7}
)
plt.title("Correlation Matrix of Measurements", fontsize=14)
plt.tight_layout()

# 4. Save the figure
out_dir = "/display_output"
png_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "correlation_matrix.png")
svg_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "correlation_matrix.svg")
plt.savefig(png_path, format="png", dpi=300)
plt.savefig(svg_path, format="svg")
plt.show()

# 5. Output description and final result
print("Correlation matrix heatmap saved as")
print(png_path)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv("input_data/measurements.csv")

# Compute the correlation matrix
corr = df.corr()

# Create a creatively coloured heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
cmap = sns.diverging_palette(220, 20, as_cmap=True)  # a vivid diverging palette
ax = sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap=cmap,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    linecolor="gray",
    cbar_kws={"shrink": .8},
    square=True,
)

ax.set_title("Correlation Matrix of Measurements", fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
png_path = "/display_output/correlation_heatmap.png"
svg_path = "/display_output/correlation_heatmap.svg"
plt.savefig(png_path, dpi=300)
plt.savefig(svg_path)

# Show the plot
plt.show()

# Description of the result
print("Correlation matrix heatmap saved as PNG and SVG in the /display_output/ folder.")

# Final result (only the PNG filename as required)
print(png_path)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv("input_data/measurements.csv")

# Compute the correlation matrix
corr = df.corr()

# Show the correlation matrix (intermediate result)
print("Correlation matrix:\n", corr)

# Create a creatively coloured heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.heatmap(
    corr,
    cmap="coolwarm",          # diverging colour map for creativity
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=0.5,
    cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.7}
)
plt.title("Correlation Matrix of Measurements", fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
png_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.png"
svg_path = "/display_output/correlation_matrix.svg"
plt.savefig(png_path, format="png", dpi=300)
plt.savefig(svg_path, format="svg")
plt.show()                     # display the plot

# Description of the result
print("Correlation matrix heatmap saved as PNG and SVG files.")

# Final output: only the filename of the PNG image
print(png_path)
